encounters.cc: Progressive dyspnea on exertion and chest tightness over 6 months

lines: Progressive dyspnea on exertion and chest tightness over 6 months

The patient is a 48-year-old male with known aortic valve stenosis, coronary artery disease, and status post renal transplantation who presents to Cardiology following recent Endocrinology evaluation.
He reports a decrease in his exercise tolerance, now becoming short of breath after walking two blocks, whereas six months ago he could jog for several miles without issue.
He denies any history of rheumatic fever.
His past medical history is significant for hypertension, controlled with lisinopril.

- Father: Coronary artery disease with MI at age 55

encounters.cc: Found unresponsive at home after recently increasing cardiac medication dose for chest discomfort

lines: Found unresponsive at home after recently increasing cardiac medication dose for chest discomfort
This 48-year-old male with aortic valve stenosis and coronary artery disease, recently evaluated for chest tightness, presents via emergency services.
According to family, he had recently increased the dose of one of his cardiac medications due to ongoing episodes of chest discomfort.
In the field, he was noted to be poorly responsive and had minimal improvement after receiving fluids.
He has a history of hypertension and coronary artery disease and has been treated with multiple agents over the years.
- Renal transplantation (living unrelated donor, 6 months prior)
- Mother: Medullary thyroid carcinoma diagnosed age 42, status post thyroidectomy
- Father: Coronary artery disease with MI at age 55
Smoking: Former smoker, 1 pack per day for 22 years, quit 8 months ago.
Alcohol: Former heavy drinker, 3-4 drinks nightly, quit 8 months ago.
Temperature 36.5°C, blood pressure 72/48 mmHg, heart rate 38/min, and respiratory rate 10/min
Cool extremities and delayed capillary refill
ECG reveals a slow rhythm with QRS prolongation
Despite multiple doses of atropine and fluid boluses, his perfusion remains poor.
He is given a medication that leads to gradual improvement in blood pressure and mental status.
